malformed

mal-FORMD · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Malformed is abnormally or badly shaped.

The x-ray revealed a malformed bone in the bird's wing, likely the result of an injury that never healed properly.

Example

The 3-D printer jammed halfway through the job, leaving behind a malformed, lopsided figurine instead of the smooth model it was supposed to make.

The figurine didn't come out the right shape at all -- it was badly, abnormally shaped, which is exactly what malformed means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

deformed: Deformed is the everyday word for a body or object that has lost or never had its normal shape, and it can sound blunt, even unkind. Malformed says the same thing in a cooler, clinical voice — the word a doctor or an engineer would reach for.

misshapen: Misshapen simply reports that a shape is wrong — a misshapen loaf, a misshapen hat — without saying how it got that way. Malformed leans clinical and points at formation: the thing took shape badly, which is why it suits medical scans and factory defects.

warped: Warped means bent or twisted out of true after it was made — heat curls a record, damp bows a bookshelf. Something malformed took its shape wrongly in the first place, as it formed or grew, rather than being a good shape spoiled later.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

symmetrical: having balanced, matching proportions

flawless: without any imperfection

Where it sits · how damaged the shape is — crooked → malformed → mutilated

crooked vs. malformed: Something crooked is only bent or uneven — a much milder flaw than malformed, which means the whole shape came out wrong.

mutilated vs. malformed: Something mutilated has been violently damaged or disfigured after the fact, a far more extreme state than malformed, which describes a shape that formed badly rather than one that was attacked.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — mal-

prefix — mal-: badly (Latin)

root — form

root — form: shape (Latin forma)

Put it together

Put it together: Malformed comes from mal- ('badly') + form ('shape', from Latin forma) -- literally 'badly shaped.' The same root form appears in dozens of common English words.

Use the root in a new word: conform

Use the root in a new word: conform: The new employee tried hard to conform to the office's unwritten dress code.

Word Choice

Malformed is a clinical, matter-of-fact word -- it's used for a shape that developed incorrectly, whether in nature, in an object, or in a plan, without necessarily implying blame.
